steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The twelve Olympian gods lived on Mount Olympus and ruled different aspects of the world

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Zeus was king of the gods, god of the sky, thunder and justice; his symbols are the thunderbolt and eagle

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Hera was queen of the gods, goddess of marriage and childbirth; she was famously jealous of Zeus's affairs

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Poseidon was god of the sea, earthquakes and horses; his symbol is the trident

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why was Zeus considered the most powerful of the Olympian gods? | Q: How did Athena's birth differ from that of other gods? | Q: Why was Ares not as widely worshipped as other gods?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Zeus was king of the gods, ruler of the sky and thunder, who overthrew the Titans to establish Olympic rule. He controlled weather, enforced justice and oaths, and other gods deferred to his authority | Athena was born fully grown and armed from Zeus's head, after he swallowed her mother Metis. She had no mother and emerged as the goddess of wisdom and strategic warfare. | Ares represented the brutal, bloodthirsty and chaotic side of war, unlike Athena who represented strategy. The Greeks valued discipline and intelligence over mindless violence.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When writing about the gods, always link their attributes to their roles Use specific myths as evidence — don't just state facts, illustrate them with stories Compare different gods' aspects when relevant — Ares vs Athena on war, for example Remember that the gods' human-like behaviour is a key feature of Greek religion The Theogony by Hesiod is the key literary source for the gods' origins and family tree
